summary:
Lunar Outpost: Mission Trainer is a free browser game for the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge. Players run a moon base for ten days, keeping oxygen, power, water and food from running out.

Players manage a crew. They send crew members with different skills to stations, choose the type of work, and discover by trial and error what each system needs. Mistakes hurt the crew and destabilize systems. When the crew are busy, players step in with hands-on minigames, such as clearing trash from a filter or filling a water tank. Story-style dialogue teaches the rules.

Daily alerts at the comms console include cyber attacks: a fake Mission Control order, phishing, an unknown USB drive, and more. The base AI explains the safe habit, and a security score ranks the player.

A lasting Moon presence will depend on teamwork and secure systems. This game teaches both to young players, for free, in any browser.
details:
WHAT IT DOES/ HOW IT WORKS:

A browser based game where you manage your lunar base for 10 days. Every night you will have 4 Life Support meters to manage (oxygen, energy, water, food). You will have a 4 person team that you will dispatch to various sections of the base (Life Support, Power Bay, Ice Rig, Greenhouse). You choose what role they will complete (Engineer, Research, Care, Security). All systems enjoy being worked however, this isn’t mentioned in the game. If you complete good tasks you will increase that system meter. However if you make mistakes you will cause damage to your team. Stability of the system will decrease. If stability reaches 0, the system will malfunction. If your team are busy or injured you can step in and complete a quick mini-game. This could include clearing trash from the air filters, re-connecting energy cables, filling the water tank to a certain amount or copying a light pattern in the greenhouse.

Everyday you will get a notification on the communication console. Some notifications will be urgent (flare). Others will be cybersecurity related (Mission Control instruction, tampered sensor, phishing email, unknown USB, default password and unverified software update). By choosing how to respond you will keep your team and base AI (ORBIT) safe. At the end you will get a security score and rank.

BENEFITS

This game is free and doesn’t require installation, account or any personal data. It can help improve your systems thinking, working within constraints and team work. It can teach you cybersecurity habits (verify, report, patch, isolate) that can be used in everyday life.

AIM

I want to help young people understand the effort needed to sustain life on the moon and how secure technology plays a part. I hope it will inspire an interest in space careers and cybersecurity. Teachers can use it in the classroom.

TOOLS/TECHNOLOGY

The game was coded using HTML, CSS and JavaScript. No framework was used, just a single file. SVG was used for the illustrations and animations within the tasks. HTML canvas was used for the particle effects. Google Fonts (Barlow & Barlow Condensed). It was hosted on GitHub pages. No special equipment was required. An AI coding assistant (Claude) was used to assist in the debugging and coding for me. I made all design decisions and drew all the character art and i especially put alot of work into juno's art.

CREATIVITY

The game includes managing your team, mini-games and a visual novel style cast who will teach you the rules. Cybersecurity threats were added to add a twist most space games wouldn’t have. The design (navy control panels, glowing meters and scanlines) and animations (team walking to sections, burst of smoke particles and day/night transitions) give it a realistic mission control feel.

THINGS TO CONSIDER

Audience: Simple rules, short game play and teaching through conversation and feedback. Accuracy: Systems are accurate to what would be needed in an outpost (air, energy, water from ice and food). The cybersecurity habits follow advice however it isn’t an official NASA simulation. Accessibility/Safety: Motion toggle can be turned off to reduce animations.Practicality: Created by me alone, so it’s a single light weight file. Quick to load and easy to host. Art: Juno portrait is hand drawn. Other art is vector graphics meaning it can be changed to custom art.
